scales.name: Barthel Index of ADL
scales.description: Independence in 10 basic activities of daily living. Widely used after stroke and in rehabilitation.
scales.instructions: Score what the patient actually does, not what they could do. Maximum 100.
scales.reference: Mahoney & Barthel, 1965 (Maryland State Medical Journal)

items.label: Feeding
items.options_text:
0|Unable
5|Needs help cutting, spreading butter, etc.
10|Independent

items.label: Bathing
items.options_text:
0|Dependent
5|Independent

items.label: Grooming
items.options_text:
0|Needs help with personal care
5|Independent (face, hair, teeth, shaving)

items.label: Dressing
items.options_text:
0|Dependent
5|Needs help but does about half unaided
10|Independent (incl. buttons, zips, laces)

items.label: Bowels
items.options_text:
0|Incontinent (or needs enemas)
5|Occasional accident
10|Continent

items.label: Bladder
items.options_text:
0|Incontinent, or catheterised and unable to manage alone
5|Occasional accident
10|Continent

items.label: Toilet use
items.options_text:
0|Dependent
5|Needs some help, can do something alone
10|Independent (on and off, dressing, wiping)

items.label: Transfers (bed to chair and back)
items.options_text:
0|Unable, no sitting balance
5|Major help (one or two people), can sit
10|Minor help (verbal or physical)
15|Independent

items.label: Mobility on level surfaces
items.options_text:
0|Immobile or < 50 yards
5|Wheelchair independent, incl. corners, > 50 yards
10|Walks with help of one person > 50 yards
15|Independent (may use any aid) > 50 yards

items.label: Stairs
items.options_text:
0|Unable
5|Needs help (verbal, physical, carrying aid)
10|Independent up and down

scales.name: Functional Independence Measure
scales.description: 18 items covering self-care, continence, transfers, locomotion, communication and social cognition. Each is graded 1-7.
scales.instructions: Grade the lowest level the patient performs on most occasions. Total 18-126.
scales.reference: FIM is a trademark of Uniform Data System for Medical Rehabilitation; confirm your clinic holds the licence required to use it.

items.label: Eating
items.options_text:

1|Total assistance (patient does < 25%)

scales.name: Modified Rankin Scale
scales.description: Global disability after stroke or other neurological injury (0-6).
scales.reference: van Swieten et al., Stroke 1988

items.label: Degree of disability
items.options_text:
0|No symptoms
1|No significant disability despite symptoms; able to carry out all usual activities
2|Slight disability; unable to carry out all previous activities but looks after own affairs without help
3|Moderate disability; needs some help but walks without assistance
4|Moderately severe disability; unable to walk or attend to bodily needs without assistance
5|Severe disability; bedridden, incontinent, needs constant nursing care
6|Dead

scales.name: Berg Balance Scale

scales.instructions: The options here are the general 0-4 grading anchors; each task has its own exact criteria (times and distances) in the published scale - grade against those. Total 0-56.
scales.reference: Berg et al., Can J Public Health 1992

scales.instructions: Record the time in seconds, with the aid used in the notes.

scales.name: Modified Ashworth Scale
scales.description: Spasticity grade for one muscle group.
scales.instructions: Assess one muscle group at a time (name it in the notes) and add another assessment for each extra muscle group.
scales.reference: Bohannon & Smith, Phys Ther 1987

items.label: Muscle tone grade
items.options_text:
0|0 - No increase in muscle tone
1|1 - Slight increase: catch and release, or minimal resistance at end of range
1.5|1+ - Slight increase: catch followed by minimal resistance through less than half of the range
2|2 - More marked increase through most of the range; part easily moved
3|3 - Considerable increase; passive movement difficult
4|4 - Affected part rigid in flexion or extension

scales.name: Muscle Strength (MRC / Oxford grade)
scales.description: Manual muscle test grade (0-5) for one muscle group.
scales.instructions: Name the muscle and side in the notes; add another assessment for each muscle you test.
scales.reference: Medical Research Council, 1943 / Oxford scale

items.label: Manual muscle test grade
items.options_text:
0|0 - No contraction
1|1 - Flicker or trace of contraction
2|2 - Active movement with gravity eliminated
3|3 - Active movement against gravity
4|4 - Active movement against gravity and some resistance
5|5 - Normal power

scales.name: Oswestry Disability Index
scales.description: Low back pain disability across 10 sections, expressed as a percentage.
scales.instructions: Each section has its own five statements in the published questionnaire; record the grade 0-5 the patient chose. One section may be skipped; the score is a percentage of the sections answered.
scales.reference: Fairbank & Pynsent, Spine 2000 (ODI v2.1a)

scales.instructions: Ask for current pain, or worst/average over the last 24 hours, and say which in the notes.

scales.description: Functional exercise capacity.
scales.instructions: Record any rest stops, the walking aid and oxygen use in the notes.
scales.reference: ATS statement, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002

scales.description: Walking speed.
scales.instructions: Speed in m/s is 10 divided by the time.
scales.reference: Perry et al., Stroke 1995

items.label: Time to walk 10 metres (seconds)
items.help_text: Time the middle 10 m of a 14 m walkway at comfortable speed.

scales.name: Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion
scales.description: How hard the patient feels they are working.

scales.name: Hand Grip Strength
scales.description: Upper-limb strength and general frailty marker.

items.label: Grip strength (kg)
items.help_text: Dynamometer, elbow at 90 degrees, best of three. Name the hand in the notes.

scales.name: Gross Motor Function Classification System
scales.description: Classifies gross motor ability of children with cerebral palsy (I = most able, V = least).
scales.instructions: The official descriptors differ by age band (under 2, 2-4, 4-6, 6-12, 12-18); classify using the band that matches the child.
scales.reference: Palisano et al., Dev Med Child Neurol 1997

items.label: GMFCS level
items.options_text:
1|Level I - Walks without limitations
2|Level II - Walks with limitations
3|Level III - Walks using a hand-held mobility device
4|Level IV - Self-mobility with limitations; may use powered mobility
5|Level V - Transported in a manual wheelchair
